changes: Cloud beat and doubled: revenue $30.7bn (+103%), operating margin 36.2% (35.6% in 2Q26), backlog $560.8bn (+$46.9bn QoQ). TPU system sales were a 'meaningful contributor' but are not sized.

Search slowed: Search & other $63.35bn, +12.0% against +16.8% in 2Q26 and flat QoQ; advertising $82.0bn vs $83.4bn expected (Reuters/LSEG). The stock fell about 13% to $281.95 by mid-morning on 29 October.

Cash burn deepened: capex $51.4bn (121% of operating cash flow), FCF -$9.1bn after -$5.9bn in 2Q26, with a $10.9bn YTD TPU inventory build and a $5.2bn EC fine. The unchanged guide implies 4Q capex of $63bn to $73bn.

Off-balance-sheet commitments jumped: leases not yet commenced $130.5bn (+53% QoQ), backstops $75.7bn ($48.0bn executed, $27.7bn to come, $10bn of it for the Blackstone JV Crux AI), energy-equipment guarantees $16.2bn (from $7.6bn), purchase commitments $924.4bn.

Funding kept flowing: $28.7bn of notes (5.55% weighted coupon, 15-year average life on the dollar tranches) and $12.4bn of ATM stock in the quarter; long-term debt $125.1bn against $46.5bn at year-end.

consensus_thesis: Investors own Alphabet as the only hyperscaler with its own full stack (TPUs, Gemini, Cloud) and pay for Cloud growing near 90% off a $514bn backlog, with external TPU sales a second engine in 2027 that justifies about $200bn of 2026 capex and $300bn or more in 2027, funded mainly by operating cash flow and Aa2/AA+ debt.
headline: The consensus view should shift from 'Cloud pays for the build' to 'Cloud is growing into a build that Search, debt and off-balance-sheet support now carry': long-term compounding holds on Cloud and TPUs, but credit quality weakens at the margin as commitments grow faster than cash generation.
kona: Google's support for third-party sites is being industrialized: $75.7bn of backstops, including $10bn reserved for Crux AI, a Blackstone joint venture selling TPU compute-as-a-service, and $16.2bn of guarantees that pre-fund counterparties' power equipment. For Kona the most realistic route to Google credit is now to host TPU systems for a Crux-type venture or an approved tenant, and to ask for an equipment guarantee on gensets rather than a lease backstop alone. The new $6.6bn TPU repurchase guarantee shows that residual-value floors are negotiable; Kona should seek one if it ever owns accelerators.

sections.body: Emphasized more: TPU systems as a platform sold through others (Oracle, Crux AI, Cirrascale); Gemini 4 Argon and Carbon; agentic commerce (UCP, Universal Cart); ROIC 'meaningfully above' cost of capital. Emphasized less or dropped: Search acceleration (now framed as lapping and FX); the 'modest' Cloud margin wording; any FCF target; the SpaceX GPU deal (not mentioned on the call). More important: inventory (TPU working capital), leases not yet commenced, backstop and guarantee totals, Search growth. Less important: headline EPS, which swings with the SpaceX mark (-$8.7bn in 3Q). Up: funding and refinancing, off-balance-sheet exposure, Search monetization in AI Mode, GPU/TPU residual value (repurchase guarantees). Down: Cloud demand, model competitiveness (Gemini 4 leads the Artificial Analysis index, per management).

sections.body: Five signals: 2027 capex number and funding mix on the January call; 4Q Cloud margin with bridging capacity; Search growth ex-FX in 4Q; Change in backstops, leases not yet commenced and guarantees; TPU revenue or unit disclosure; inventory turning to revenue. Key risks building: Cash: FCF negative two quarters with 4Q capex stepping up. Balance sheet: about $229bn of leases, backstops and guarantees outside reported debt. Search: slower growth as AI Mode scales. Confirmation signals: Cloud margin holds above 33% in 4Q; TPU inventory converts to revenue in 1H27; Search re-accelerates once ads scale in AI Mode. Conviction tripwires: 2027 capex above $330bn without an FCF floor; any further equity beyond the ATM; a backstop being called; Cloud margin below 30%.
sections.title: Monitoring checklist

head: Type
Question
Why it matters / was it asked
rows: Backstops rose to $75.7bn: $48.0bn executed plus $27.7bn you must still put in place, $10bn for Crux AI. How many counterparties and MW does that cover, what share is with unrated neoclouds, and do your rating agencies count it as debt? Yes or no.
Asked? No. It is the largest debt-like item outside the balance sheet and sets how far Google's credit reaches across the sector.
Leases not yet commenced rose $45.3bn in one quarter to $130.5bn. How much commences in 2027, and what is lease-adjusted net leverage at year-end 2027 on your plan?
Asked? No. Commencements turn into finance-lease debt and fixed costs ahead of revenue.

You told us in July you would not return to equity markets beyond the ATM for employee tax. You sold $12.4bn in 3Q. What is the 2027 debt issuance range, and is there a leverage ceiling that would trigger more equity?
Asked? No. Sets the bond supply overhang and dilution risk.
Your guide implies 4Q capex of $63bn to $73bn after $51.4bn in 3Q. What share is servers vs buildings and power, and how much is TPU systems for sale (inventory) rather than your own fleet?
Asked in part (Sandler): answered as an inventory cycle, no numbers.
You disclosed $6.6bn of guarantees to repurchase sold TPU hardware. At what discount to cost, over what term, and how does that compare with expected TPU resale values after a first contract?
Asked? No. It is a residual-value floor that moves chip risk back to Google.
Cloud margin was 36.2% because bridging capacity arrived late. What is the 4Q cost of that capacity and its MW, and when does owned capacity replace it?
